name: permission-scope
body: The per-path scope under which an agent's write (edit or filesystem operation) is permitted: the agent's EFFECTIVE `edit`-action scope — the ordered combination of the lower-priority configuration, the global rules, and the agent's own opencode 2.x `permissions` entries, with the last matching rule winning — where an allow rule grants the path and a deny rule revokes it. opencode resolves a path that matches zero rules to `ask`; a deny or a rejection refuses the operation, so a filesystem operation is fail-closed (per `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`) and cannot reach a path the `edit` action denies. For a CODE-WRITER the scope is WORKTREE-ROOTED — its globs name `apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>` paths only, with a main-checkout path outside them — so the grant covers exactly the project worktree the agent mutates and main stays read-only to it; `external_directory` governs an out-of-worktree path. The only scopes that reach the main checkout belong to the carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` (the agent-builder's `.opencode/agents/**`; the optional release-agent's per-repo release artefacts). It is the agent's owned surface expressed for path matching — narrow by construction (deny-by-default, exactly the source/config/test globs the role owns), a bounded capability. A path outside the scope, or one a later deny revokes, is refused.
